content.comment_body: How can I change the off-delay time setting on “B001” for the [product_name]? I notice it takes the value from B012 and updates the T time for “B001”, but not the Ta value. The display on the [product_name] shows the correct value, but the off-delay time Ta does not actually change. What is the recommended way to adjust this properly?

The "Ta" parameter is an output of a timer block and cannot be modified directly. It represents the elapsed portion of the input parameter "T" (initial value). Only the input parameter "T" can be changed using reference functions. Additionally, the time unit is milliseconds—70 ms equals 0.07 seconds.

Thanks for the details and for sharing the video. 0.7 s is what I want set as the default value. I would like this to be adjustable on the [product_name] using its buttons, similar to how the value for B005 can be changed using buttons, since B002 & B005 are counters. Is there a way to make B001’s off-delay time adjustable via button presses? Any suggestions?
Just to clarify, 70 ms is actually 0.07 seconds—not 0.7 seconds.

You can display the off-delay time for B001 in the message text and adjust the off-delay parameter from there. Here’s how: In the correct message text, hold ESC for 2 seconds—this changes the cursor to a black bar. Use up/down to select the field you want to modify. Press OK; the cursor becomes a flashing box. Adjust the number with up/down, move digit position with left/right. When done, press OK. The cursor turns back to a black bar. To exit, press the ESC key.

Correct! Thanks [user_name]. It’s now set to tx (ten milliseconds), as shown in your video. Still, I need a way to adjust the time delay directly with the buttons. Has anyone seen an example program for [product_name] where the off-delay time can be changed by pressing the device buttons?
Please refer to my last thread where I’ve attached a second video.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is trying to adjust the off-delay time (Ta) of a timer block on a [product_name] device using the device's buttons. There was initial confusion about which parameters could be changed, as only the main time (T) can be adjusted, but Ta cannot since it is an output parameter. Other users clarified this and explained how adjustments can be made through the message text interface and offered procedural steps for changing the value via the device’s buttons.
analysis.user_expectations: The user would like to intuitively adjust the off-delay time (Ta) on the [product_name] via button presses, similar to modifying counter values, and is looking for straightforward, on-device solutions.
